 """Clean up the contacts export before it goes into the mailing tool."""
 import csv
+from datetime import date
 
 
 def read_contacts(path):
@@ -18,6 +19,41 @@ def tidy(row):
     }
 
 
+def _updated_key(row):
+    """Sortable date for a tidied row. Expects ISO dates (YYYY-MM-DD).
+
+    A blank value sorts as older than any real date. Any other format raises
+    ValueError rather than guessing, so a wrong date format cannot silently
+    keep the stale row.
+    """
+    value = row["updated"]
+    if not value:
+        return date.min
+    try:
+        return date.fromisoformat(value[:10])
+    except ValueError:
+        raise ValueError(
+            "cannot read 'updated' value %r for %s; expected YYYY-MM-DD"
+            % (value, row["email"])
+        ) from None
+
+
 def clean(rows):
-    """The clean-up step run on every export."""
-    return [tidy(row) for row in rows]
+    """The clean-up step run on every export.
+
+    Rows with the same email (ignoring case and surrounding spaces) are the
+    same person; the row with the latest 'updated' date is kept. On a tie the
+    first row in the file wins. Rows with a blank email are never merged.
+    """
+    out = []
+    position = {}  # email -> index in out
+    for row in map(tidy, rows):
+        email = row["email"]
+        if not email:
+            out.append(row)
+        elif email not in position:
+            position[email] = len(out)
+            out.append(row)
+        elif _updated_key(row) > _updated_key(out[position[email]]):
+            out[position[email]] = row
+    return out

 import contacts

 def test_tidy_trims_and_lowercases():

@@ -23,3 +29,62 @@ def test_read_contacts(tmp_path):
     p.write_text("name,email,phone,updated\nAnn,ann@x.org,1,2024-01-10\n",
                  encoding="utf-8")
     assert contacts.read_contacts(p)[0]["email"] == "ann@x.org"
+

+def test_duplicates_ignore_case_and_spaces_latest_wins():

+    ]
+    out = contacts.clean(rows)
+    assert len(out) == 1
+    assert out[0]["phone"] == "new"
+    assert out[0]["email"] == "foo@x.com"
+
+
+def test_latest_wins_even_if_it_comes_first_in_file():
+    rows = [
+        _row("Foo new", "foo@x.com", phone="new", updated="2024-03-05"),
+        _row("Foo old", "FOO@x.com", phone="old", updated="2024-01-10"),
+    ]
+    out = contacts.clean(rows)
+    assert [r["phone"] for r in out] == ["new"]
+
+
+def test_tie_keeps_first_in_file():
+    rows = [
+        _row("First", "foo@x.com", updated="2024-01-10"),
+        _row("Second", "Foo@x.com", updated="2024-01-10"),
+    ]
+    assert [r["name"] for r in contacts.clean(rows)] == ["First"]
+
+
+def test_output_order_follows_first_appearance():
+    rows = [
+        _row("Ann", "ann@x.org", updated="2024-01-01"),
+        _row("Bob", "bob@x.org", updated="2024-01-01"),
+        _row("Ann again", "ANN@x.org", updated="2024-02-01"),
+    ]
+    assert [r["name"] for r in contacts.clean(rows)] == ["Ann again", "Bob"]
+
+
+def test_blank_emails_are_not_merged():
+    rows = [_row("A", ""), _row("B", "  ")]
+    assert len(contacts.clean(rows)) == 2
+
+
+def test_blank_updated_is_older_than_a_real_date():
+    rows = [
+        _row("Dated", "foo@x.com", updated="2020-01-01"),
+        _row("Blank", "foo@x.com", updated=""),
+    ]
+    assert [r["name"] for r in contacts.clean(rows)] == ["Dated"]
+
+
+def test_unreadable_date_in_duplicate_group_raises():
+    rows = [
+        _row("A", "foo@x.com", updated="01/02/2024"),
+        _row("B", "foo@x.com", updated="2024-01-10"),
+    ]
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="01/02/2024"):
+        contacts.clean(rows)
